1	Parking structures, fleet depots, workplaces and multi unit dwellings commonly install several electric vehicle connectors on a single electrical branch. The conductors, overcurrent device and upstream transformer capacity of that branch are sized for an aggregate current that is lower, and often much lower, than the sum of the individual current ratings of the connectors served by it. The installation therefore depends on a control function that continuously divides the branch capacity among the connectors that are in use, rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit to each vehicle over a control pilot signalling interface. The limit is advisory in the sense that it is a request addressed to equipment that the site operator does not own and cannot inspect. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous current for an interval after a new limit is signalled, or may not follow the signalled limit at all. Auxiliary equipment on the same branch, such as lighting, ventilation, elevators or refrigeration, draws current that the charging control function does not command and that changes without notice. A control function that computes an allocation and then assumes the allocation has taken effect can therefore hold the branch above its rated aggregate current while every connector believes it is compliant, with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection. Tripping that device removes every charging session on the branch at once, and in many installations it also removes the auxiliary loads sharing the branch.
4	
5	Site controllers of this class also depend on a network connection to a remote management service for schedules, tariffs and driver authorization. Connectivity in a below grade parking structure or a remote depot is intermittent. A controller that treats loss of connectivity as a reason to stop charging strands vehicles that were already authorized, while a controller that treats loss of connectivity as permission to charge without restraint abandons the branch limit that the last accepted configuration established, and abandons the accounting record that billing depends on.
6	
7	A further difficulty arises at installation. The connector identifier used by the control function, the physical contactor that energizes a connector and the current sensing channel that measures it are joined by field wiring performed once, often by a contractor who does not operate the equipment afterwards. If that wiring map is recorded incorrectly, the control function will deliver a computed current limit to one connector while measuring another. Every subsequent verification appears to succeed, because the two errors are consistent with one another, and the fault is discovered only when the branch overcurrent device operates or when a vehicle receives a limit that was intended for a different vehicle.
8	
9	There remains a need for a controller that treats the aggregate current of the branch as a measured quantity, verified independently of the per connector measurements and independently of any vehicle response, and that converts an unanswered current reduction into a bounded, ordered and recoverable removal of load rather than into an uncontrolled trip of the branch overcurrent device.

Each connector channel of the apparatus includes a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective vehicle connector, a connector current sensor arranged to measure a connector current delivered through that vehicle connector, and a control-pilot interface, and each connector channel is associated with a local connector identifier. A branch current sensor is arranged to measure a branch current in the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector channels, so that the aggregate current of the branch is obtained from a measurement that is independent of the per connector measurements.
2	
3	A controller is coupled to the control-pilot interfaces, to the contactors and to the branch current sensor. The controller stores, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. At each allocation interval of a succession of allocation intervals, the controller subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current, assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. The controller sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel and verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel.
4	
5	The branch current sensor serves as an independent safety input. Responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for a verification interval after a reduced pilot command has been sent, the controller opens the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a bounded and predetermined sequence, and only to the extent that the measured branch current shows the removal to be necessary, rather than by operation of the branch overcurrent device.
6	
7	In further aspects, a contactor is not reclosed until the connector current sensor of its connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not restore load simultaneously. A welded-contactor condition is recorded when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, whereupon the controller inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch and operates a local fault indicator.

During a network outage the controller continues already authorized charging sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to the branch current sensing described above, and does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and has not expired. Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.
4	
5	A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.
6	
7	An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller, is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.
8

The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value by which the edge controller 106 addresses that connector channel over the isolated local bus 108 and under which it stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel.

11	The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. 19	At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.
20	
21	At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained. 22

32

34	
35	At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.
36	
37	The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.
38	
39	During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. 40	
41	Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence at the edge controller 106. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.
42

46	
47	The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling.
48
